headline: Japanese 101 Foundation 10
threshold: Practice everyday Japanese with English support; lesson completion is not a proficiency credential.

lessons.title: Hello and your name
lessons.objective: Hello and your name: Hear the five Japanese vowels あ・い・う・え・お. Use a polite greeting and ～です for a name; は marks the topic and is pronounced wa here. Add か at the end to make a polite question.
lessons.focus: Hear the five Japanese vowels あ・い・う・え・お. Use a polite greeting and ～です for a name; は marks the topic and is pronounced wa here. Add か at the end to make a polite question.

lessons.speaking: Role-play meeting a classmate with a patient Japanese-speaking partner. Use the lesson's polite forms, ask and answer a related question, clarify one misunderstanding, and close naturally. Give brief English help when requested.

lessons.title: This and that
lessons.objective: This and that: Practice hiragana in short nouns. これ is this (near me), それ is that (near you), and あれ is that over there. この goes before a noun; の connects nouns or marks possession. Japanese nouns have no articles or grammatical gender.

words.en: The pencil is on the desk.

lessons.title: One or several
lessons.objective: One or several: Keep practicing hiragana and recognize katakana in loanwords (ノート, ゴム). Japanese nouns usually do not change for plural; quantity and context tell us how many. Use ～つ for general items such as erasers; bound notebooks use ～さつ (にさつ means two notebooks). The object particle を is pronounced o. も means also or too and replaces は or を.

lessons.title: Who is speaking?
lessons.objective: Who is speaking?: Use a name or わたし when needed, but notice that Japanese often omits a subject clear from context. Ask どなたですか politely for who; だれですか is less formal. Use ～さん politely after a person's name.

lessons.title: Identity and origin
lessons.objective: Identity and origin: Use ～です for identity or role and ～から きました for where someone came from. は introduces the topic; が can identify the person answering who, but keep the contrast contextual.
lessons.focus: Use ～です for identity or role and ～から きました for where someone came from. は introduces the topic; が can identify the person answering who, but keep the contrast contextual.

words.es: わたしは マリです。
にほんから きました。

words.en: Ken, where did you come from?

words.es: アメリカから きました。
words.en: I came from the United States.

words.es: せんせいは どなたですか。

lessons.title: Where people and things are
lessons.objective: Where people and things are: Use あります for inanimate things and います for people or animals. に marks where something exists; ここ, そこ, and あそこ locate it.

words.es: けんさんは どこに いますか。
あの へやに います。
いすは どこに ありますか。
ねこも へやに いますか。
words.en: Is the cat in the room too?

words.es: いいえ、ねこは あそこに います。
words.en: No, the cat is over there.

lessons.title: What is in the room?
lessons.objective: What is in the room?: Ask ～に なにが ありますか about things and ～に だれが いますか about people. Reuse the あります/います contrast and location words without treating them as interchangeable.
lessons.focus: Ask ～に なにが ありますか about things and ～に だれが いますか about people. Reuse the あります/います contrast and location words without treating them as interchangeable.

words.es: へやに なにが ありますか。
つくえと いすが あります。
words.en: There is a desk and a chair.

words.es: まどの となりに ドアが あります。
words.en: There is a door next to the window.

words.es: へやに だれが いますか。

words.en: The meeting is in this room.

lessons.title: Numbers, age, and counters
lessons.objective: Numbers, age, and counters: Read numbers one to ten. なんにん means how many people; いくつ means how many general items. Use ～さい（歳） for age and an appropriate counter for objects; ～つ counts general items, while ～にん（人） counts people. Some readings change, including ひとり（一人）. に (two) sounds the same as the location particle に; さん (three) sounds the same as the polite name suffix. 18 is じゅうはち, but 18 years old is じゅうはっさい.

words.es: がくせいは なんにん いますか。
ペンは いくつ ありますか。
けんさんは なんさいですか。

lessons.title: Ask and say no
lessons.objective: Ask and say no: Add か to make a polite question. Say いいえ for no and use じゃありません for a negative noun sentence (more formal: では ありません); polite verb negatives use ～ません.

lessons.title: Ask for help and review
lessons.objective: Ask for help and review: Keep a conversation going with わかりません, もういちど おねがいします, and ゆっくり おねがいします. Review the polite questions, quantity, and existence forms from Foundation.
